Title: Superior Faceless Night vs. action fails

Messages.Author: AaronC
Messages.Body:
Does the effect of superior Faceless Night still apply to blocking minions if the action fails?

The card text says the tapping happens when the action resolves. Does a fizzled action resolve?

This question came up in a tournament this weekend when one my prey's Imbued attempted to block my vampire with . I played superior Faceless Night, and the block was unsuccessful. I played a bleed modifier, then one of my prey's Imbued used Champion to cause the action to fail (and start a combat between the two minions). The judge ruled that the first minion attempting to block was still tapped by superior Faceless Night. There are many reasons an action can fail, but I couldn't find a ruling about this.

Faceless Night
[Action Modifier] Action Modifier
[obf] +1 stealth.
[OBF] +1 stealth, and any minion who attempts to block this action and fails becomes tapped when the action is resolved (before resolving the action).
You are eternity's hostage,
a captive of time.
Boris Pasternak, Night

Champion
Power
Defense
[REACTION] [2 CONVICTION] Only usable when a monster controlled by another Methuselah is taking a  action against you or against an imbued controlled by any player. The action fails and the acting monster enters combat with this imbued instead.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
When an action is blocked, the combat generated by the block is the resolution of the action.
All actions resolve, except those that are canceled.

Faceless Night taps minions who failed to successfully block, regardless of what happens to the action.  [LSJ 19990526] (this is based on the "old" text of Faceless Night, which was explicit. LSJ confirms the new text is not an errata to the old one here:  [LSJ 20020321] )

Examples: A blocked Force of Will will inflict its agg damage after that combat.
Seraph's Second is usable if the acting Black Hand was blocked.

Messages.Author: henrik
Messages.Body:
> Pascal wrote:
> Faceless Night taps minions who failed to successfully block, regardless of what happens to the action.  [LSJ 19990526] (this is based on the "old" text of Faceless Night, which was explicit. LSJ confirms the new text is not an errata to the old one here:  [LSJ 20020321] )
>
According to those rulings, Faceless Night does not (as it should, according to it's card text) wait until action resolution to tap the relevant minion/s.

From  [LSJ 19990526] :
>
> (It taps an unsuccessful blocker when the controller declares "no more block attempts" or when another minion's block is successful.)
>
Further confirmation here:
[LSJ 20000814]

I think card text should probably be changed to "after block attempts are resolved or declined" or something along those lines, instead of the current "when the action is resolved (before resolving the action)".

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
Current cardtext (which was changed in 2002, and caused the second link's discussion) changed Faceless Night so that
- it wouldn't tap minions who successfully block (matters for Atonement)
- it taps minions at resolution (rather than when their block attempt fails)

This brings up a point:
What is the reasoning that an action that is "ended" doesn't bring the action immediately to IV.E (thus allowing action mods to be played)? Was it before and/or is it now important to have a distinction between action "ends" and action "fail"?

"If action was blocked, the action is unsuccessful and blocked."

Messages.Author: AaronC
Messages.Body:
Okay, obviously you can't play Freak Drive after an "action fails" effect, but is there a window for playing "action ends" cards?

According to Kevin there is, but I don't see any rules references or rulings to back that up.

"Action ends" specifically sounds like it would go to the end-of-the-action timing window in a way similar to "combat ends" effects taking you to the end-of-the-round/end-of-combat windows.

"Action fails" sounds like it would do exactly the same thing as "action ends". Would love to see a reference as to how they're different.

Messages.Author: AaronC
Messages.Body:
Did you check the rules reference before posting, I wonder? If card text says when something happens, then it describes the timing window. Using that timing window is outlined in the reference.

Combat is part of resolving a blocked action. After the combat resolves you play effects that occur at the end of the action, like superior Freak Drive or Provision of the Silsila.

If you dispensed with the "as above" clause, the superior Freak Drive text could read as "Only usable at the end of an action (after resolving the action or combat, if any)." That's the "action ends" window I'm talking about that the rules reference mentions in IV.E.

Getting back to topic, I still would like to see more documentation about the difference between 'action ends' and 'action fails' that Kevin describes. I want more evidence about the fate of the 'action ends' window when applied to 'action ends' or 'action fails' effects.
